intro: Spanish has several verbs for «become». Each one tells a different kind of change.
p.me puse.glosa: I got; I became (for a while)
p.me puse.consejo: «Ponerse» + adjective tells a passing state, often a reaction: «me puse rojo».
p.se volvió.consejo: «Volverse» + adjective speaks of a lasting change of character: «se volvió muy serio».
p.se hizo.consejo: «Hacerse» + noun tells a choice or a path: «se hizo médica».
p.se quedó.consejo: «Quedarse» shows the state you end up in: «se quedó sin trabajo», «me quedé sorprendido».
p.se convirtió en.consejo: It always takes «en» and a noun: «se convirtió en una estrella».
p.llegó a ser.glosa: came to be; ended up as
p.llegó a ser.consejo: It tells an achievement after a process: «llegó a ser campeona». The ll sounds like y.
p.nervioso.consejo: It changes with the person: «nervioso» for him, «nerviosa» for her. «Ponerse nervioso» is very common.
p.famoso.consejo: The stress is on «MO»: fa-MO-so. It changes with gender: «famoso», «famosa».
p.rojo.consejo: The initial r sounds strong and the j like h: RRO-ho. «Ponerse rojo» means to blush.
p.cantante.consejo: It works for a man and a woman: «un cantante», «una cantante». Only the article changes.
p.estrella.consejo: The ll sounds like y: es-TRE-ya. It has two meanings: the one in the sky and the famous person.
p.médica.consejo: The accent marks the stress: ME-di-ka. For a man, «médico».
b1.texto:
English says «become» or «get». Spanish chooses according to the change:

- **Ponerse** + adjective: a passing state. **Me puse nervioso.**
- **Volverse** + adjective: a lasting change of character. **Se volvió muy serio.**
- **Hacerse** + noun: a profession or a belief. **Se hizo médica.**
- **Quedarse** + adjective: the state you end up in. **Se quedó sin trabajo.**
- **Convertirse en** + noun: a transformation. **Se convirtió en una estrella.**

And **llegar a ser** tells an achievement: **llegó a ser campeona.**
b2.f1.texto: He became a singer and got very famous.
b2.f2.texto: In class he always went red when he spoke.
b2.f3.texto: Now he has turned into a music star.
b2.f5.texto: He became very rich before he was thirty.
b2.f6.texto: I got nervous when I saw him on TV.
b2.f7.texto: I became calmer with the years.
b4.texto:
- **ponerse** + adjective → a passing state: Me puse rojo.
- **volverse** + adjective → a lasting change of character: Se volvió muy serio.
- **hacerse** + noun or adjective → a profession or an identity: Se hizo abogada.
- **quedarse** + adjective → the result of something: Se quedó sin trabajo.
- **convertirse en** + noun → a transformation: Se convirtió en un héroe.
- **llegar a ser** → an achievement after a process: Llegó a ser campeona.

Some changes have their own verb: **enfadarse**, **alegrarse**, **envejecer**, **engordar**.
b4.e0.texto: I got nervous in the interview.
b4.e1.texto: My neighbour was left without a job.
b4.e2.texto: Her sister became a swimming champion.
b5.f0.texto: The theatre falls silent when the lights go out.
b5.f1.texto: A white spotlight falls on the stage and draws a circle of golden dust.
b5.f2.texto: Marcos appears with his guitar and goes red under the applause.
b5.f3.texto: For a second he looks like the same shy boy from the music class.
b5.f4.texto: Then he closes his eyes, breathes deeply and starts to sing in a big, clear voice.
b5.f5.texto: When the song ends, the audience stands up.
b5.f6.texto: Marcos smiles, wipes his forehead with his sleeve and makes a little bow.
b5.f7.texto: He is no longer the boy who used to hide behind the door.
b5.f8.texto: Time has turned him into a calm, confident star.
b5.f9.texto: Among the audience, Lucía and Pablo are left speechless and can only clap.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Ponerse» + adjective tells a passing state.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Hacerse» is for a profession or identity, not for a moment of nerves.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Volverse» is a lasting change of character, not a moment.
b6.pregunta: It is a passing state. Which verb goes here?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Ponerse» is for passing states; a profession is not one.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Hacerse» + profession tells the chosen path.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Quedarse» shows the result of something, not a chosen career.
b7.pregunta: Which sentence speaks of a new profession?
b8.frase: Se hizo cantante y se volvió famoso
b8.traduccion: He became a singer and got famous
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Hacerse» suggests a choice, and nobody chooses to lose a job.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Volverse» changes character; here the situation changes.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! «Quedarse» shows the state you end up in.
b9.pregunta: It is the result of something that happened. Which verb?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Llegar a ser» tells a goal reached over time.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Ponerse» is for a state of a moment, not for a title.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Quedarse campeona» does not tell the effort or the path.
b10.pregunta: Which sentence tells an achievement after a lot of effort?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «She became a doctor».
b12.o0.refuerzo: A change for good would ask for «me volví» or «me hice».
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is a long process: «llegué a ser», «me hice».
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is it! «Ponerse» tells something passing, like embarrassment.
b12.pregunta: «Me puse rojo». How long does the change last?
p.convertido.consejo: Past participle of «convertir». The «v» sounds like «b».
p.campeona.consejo: Feminine of «campeón». The ending «-a» shows a woman.
p.apagan.consejo: «Apagar» means to turn off. «Se apagan» here means the lights go off.
p.foco.consejo: A light that shines on one spot of the stage. The «c» sounds like «k».
p.pie.consejo: «De pie» means standing up. Say «PYE», with «ie» as one sound.
p.manga.consejo: The sleeve of a shirt. The «g» before «a» is hard.
p.reverencia.consejo: A respectful bow. The «v» sounds like «b», and «cia» is «thya» in Spain.
p.escondía.consejo: Imperfect of «esconder». It describes a habit in the past.
p.aplaudir.consejo: Infinitive of «aplaudir». It follows «solo pueden», as in «can only applaud».
p.quedó.consejo: Past tense of «quedar», for «él» or «ella». It can mean she was left speechless.
